question: How does money move between Treasury, the Fed, the GSEs, the trust funds and the IMF?
answer: The federal tree records 16 money relationships among 20 bodies. 10 of them run through the Treasury: 8 point into it (revenue in, customs receipts / approved refunds, profits remitted, holds the public debt, intragovernmental IOUs, conservatorship dividends) and 2 point out (quota / dues (up & out), backstop / guarantee). The other 6 are seized assets, internal lending, quota / dues (up & out), ownership capital & dividends, state equity stakes. None of the 16 is dated in the master.

sections.title: Flow by flow, with the explanation printed
sections.sub: → one way, ⇄ both ways. The explanation is the federal tree's own sentence.

items.title: Assets Forfeiture Fund → Strategic Bitcoin Reserve
items.text: Seized bitcoin, consolidated into the permanent reserve.
kv: From Assets Forfeiture Fund to Strategic Bitcoin Reserve

items.title: Assets Forfeiture Fund → US Digital Asset Stockpile
items.text: Other seized digital assets, swept into the stockpile.
kv: From Assets Forfeiture Fund to US Digital Asset Stockpile

items.title: IRS → Dept of the Treasury
items.text: Internal tax revenue — the group's main income.
kv: From IRS to Dept of the Treasury

items.title: External Revenue Service (proposed) → Dept of the Treasury
items.text: Proposed tariff revenue — but the collector doesn't legally exist yet.
kv: From External Revenue Service (proposed) to Dept of the Treasury

items.title: Fannie Mae → Dept of the Treasury
items.text: Conservatorship dividends swept to Treasury since 2008.
kv: From Fannie Mae to Dept of the Treasury

items.title: Freddie Mac → Dept of the Treasury
kv: From Freddie Mac to Dept of the Treasury

items.title: Dept of the Treasury ⇄ IMF
items.text: The US quota — paid in and drawn on via the Exchange Stabilization Fund.

items.title: The Federal Reserve System ⇄ Bank for International Settlements
items.text: The Fed is the US seat at the central banks' bank.

items.title: CBP ⇄ Dept of the Treasury
items.text: CBP assesses, collects, liquidates, and reviews customs duties and refund claims; Treasury recognizes customs revenue and issues approved refunds. The reverse arrow is the refund instruction/accounting handoff — Treasury pays the claimant, not CBP — and does not prove a specific electronic route into the Treasury General Account.

items.title: The Federal Reserve System → Dept of the Treasury
items.text: Reserve Banks remit residual net earnings to Treasury. During a loss period, each Bank records its own deferred asset and suspends remittances until that Bank's cumulative earnings recover the balance; current public statements do not establish one Systemwide restart date.
kv: From The Federal Reserve System to Dept of the Treasury

items.title: The Federal Reserve System → Dept of the Treasury
items.text: The Fed (via the SOMA desk) holds trillions in Treasury debt — it finances the parent.
kv: From The Federal Reserve System to Dept of the Treasury

items.title: Social Security Trust Funds (OASI + DI) ⇄ Dept of the Treasury
items.text: Surpluses buy special Treasuries; interest is paid back. An IOU the group writes to itself.
kv: Social Security Trust Funds (OASI + DI) founded

items.title: Federal Financing Bank → Government corporations
items.text: Treasury's in-house bank lends to agencies and buys their debt.
kv: From Federal Financing Bank to Government corporations

items.title: ≈2,000 member banks (statutory stock subscribers) ⇄ The 12 Federal Reserve Banks
items.text: Member banks subscribe nontransferable statutory Reserve Bank stock: $100 par per share, half paid and half subject to call, with a cumulative semiannual two-tier dividend. The stock is not ordinary corporate ownership and does not convey control of the Reserve Bank System.

items.title: Dept of the Treasury → FDIC
items.text: A Treasury line of credit backstops the deposit-insurance fund.
kv: From Dept of the Treasury to FDIC

items.title: US Sovereign Wealth Fund → US Investment Accelerator
items.text: The 'fund' has no body — it invests through this Commerce office, deal by deal.
kv: From US Sovereign Wealth Fund to US Investment Accelerator

uncertain: None of the 16 flows carries a date or a source link in the master. The 'evidence through' stamp is the newest founding date among the bodies drawn (March 31, 2025), so the list is at least that recent; when each flow was last checked is not recorded.
A flow says money can move this way; it does not give amounts or prove a particular payment.
The External Revenue Service is proposed and does not legally exist yet; the US Sovereign Wealth Fund has no body of its own.
sources: Master: Workbench masters/federal_entities.json, the flows list and its legend of kinds (the federal tree's one home, DR-104).

pictures.title: The money map, on the federal tree
pictures.sub: Each box is a legal body from the federal tree, drawn inside the department, regulator or Fed body that owns it. Counting the bodies that sit inside Treasury, 13 of the 16 recorded relationships touch the Treasury group. The Fed's own capital and BIS ties sit under the Fed; the sovereign-fund route sits at the foot of the right column.

cols.label: Treasury and the bodies inside it

boxes.label: Inside the Treasury
boxes.note: The money parent — issues the debt, runs disbursement, custodies the new digital-asset vehicles, and chairs the councils that watch the whole financial system.

boxes.label: Treasury (the department)
boxes.note: The money parent — issues the debt, runs disbursement, custodies the new digital-asset vehicles, and chairs the councils that watch the whole financial system.

boxes.label: External Revenue Service (proposed)
boxes.note: Announced to collect tariffs and foreign-source revenue — but it cannot be created without Congress, so as of 2026 it is a name, not an entity.

boxes.label: Federal Financing Bank
boxes.note: A Treasury-owned bank that lends to other federal agencies and buys their debt.

boxes.label: Strategic Bitcoin Reserve
boxes.note: Permanent Treasury-held BTC reserve, chartered by EO, seeded with forfeited bitcoin. Still fighting to become statute.

boxes.label: US Digital Asset Stockpile
boxes.note: Sister vehicle holding non-bitcoin forfeited digital assets under Treasury.

boxes.label: IRS
boxes.note: Revenue collection.

boxes.label: The Federal Reserve System
boxes.note: The central bank — chartered by Congress (Federal Reserve Act, 23 Dec 1913) but not owned or run by the executive. Public head, private body.

boxes.label: The 12 Federal Reserve Banks
boxes.note: Regional banks that are private corporations, their stock held by the member commercial banks (opened 16 Nov 1914).

boxes.label: ≈2,000 member banks
boxes.note: National banks and state member banks that subscribe the statutory capital stock of their district Reserve Bank.

boxes.label: Bank for International Settlements
boxes.note: The central banks' bank, in Basel — the oldest international financial institution.

boxes.label: Dept of Justice
boxes.note: Runs federal forfeiture — the pipeline that fed seized bitcoin into the new Treasury reserve.

boxes.label: Assets Forfeiture Fund
boxes.note: Holds proceeds of seizure.

boxes.label: Dept of Homeland Security
boxes.note: Internal offices shut down March 2025 (Civil Rights & Civil Liberties, two ombudsmen).

boxes.label: FHFA
boxes.note: Regulator AND conservator of Fannie & Freddie since 2008 — drawn here as their parent-of-record WHILE the conservatorship lasts.

boxes.label: Fannie Mae
boxes.note: Federally chartered mortgage giant, private shareholders — in FHFA conservatorship since Sep 2008. Treasury holds senior preferred stock + warrants for 79.9% of the common.

boxes.label: Government corporations
boxes.note: Entities literally chartered as corporations — own charter, own board, own balance sheet.

boxes.label: FDIC
boxes.note: Deposit insurer with its own fund built from bank premiums — a corporation inside the regulatory layer.

boxes.label: Freddie Mac
boxes.note: Sister GSE, also in FHFA conservatorship since Sep 2008 — same Treasury stake, same limbo.

boxes.label: IMF
boxes.note: The US is the largest quota-holder and the only member with a veto.

boxes.label: Social Security Trust Funds (OASI + DI)
boxes.note: Intragovernmental IOUs (OASI 1940, DI 1956).

boxes.label: US Sovereign Wealth Fund
boxes.note: Directed by EO Feb 2025; a plan was delivered, but no single legal entity was stood up. It went decentralized — stakes taken agency by agency, largely through the Commerce Investment Accelerator.

boxes.label: Dept of Commerce
boxes.note: Home of the new Investment Accelerator — the office the Sovereign Wealth Fund is actually operating through.

boxes.label: US Investment Accelerator
boxes.note: New Commerce office (EO 14255) to fast-track $1B+ investments — the real mechanism behind the decentralized 'sovereign wealth fund'.
